chapter: Philadelphia and the move to New York
title: Working with Charlie Parker
summary: Bryant knew the records so Parker could just call key and tempo; Parker liked him and planned to record with him.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: So as a house pianist, if the manager said to you okay — how much warning did you have, or I wouldn’t say warning, how much time did you have before you knew a particular guy was coming to play, and did you feel you had to do some homework somehow to research the tunes that you knew that they liked to play? Or did you just have enough knowledge at that time where you could go in.

Well I think I had the knowledge, because I of course listened to all their records. I had the records of Charlie Parker, and I listened to nothing but jazz recordings from guys at the time. And so like when I went in to play with Charlie Parker I knew all the tunes and he would just call out the key and set the tempo and we’d go.
Was he personable to work with?

Very personable. Yes. Charlie was a nice guy. I know he liked me. And we had a very good time together. As a matter of fact we were going to record together, because he said on my next recording session I want you guys. And he passed away.
